source.title: ADAHESSIAN: An Adaptive Second Order Optimizer for Machine Learning
source.authors: Zhe-Wei Yao; A. Gholami; Sheng Shen; M. Mustafa; K. Keutzer; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the results used here.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports optimizer outcomes on several benchmarks, including training-loss and accuracy comparisons, but does not test the claim versions about zero or near-zero training classification error, bad local minima, shortcuts, initialization, stability limits, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The reported AdaHessian/optimizer comparisons concern generalization metrics (accuracy, BLEU, PPL, CTR) and training loss, not training classification error or the specific conditions named in the claim versions. These results do not meet the row criterion for this claim.
record.test_reason: The study compares optimizers, but its own results do not test any specified version. CIFAR-10 figures report training loss and test accuracy, not training classification error. Learning-rate sweeps do not establish stability thresholds or recovery dynamics. There are no controlled comparisons of width, shortcuts, initialization, or batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: AdaHessian achieves comparable or better generalization than tuned default optimizers across the evaluated tasks, with a typical per-iteration runtime cost of roughly 2–3× that of first-order methods. Delaying Hessian updates reduces this overhead with small accuracy changes.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces AdaHessian, a stochastic adaptive second-order optimizer using a Hutchinson estimate of the Hessian diagonal, spatial averaging, and Hessian momentum; comparisons are against SGD, Adam, AdamW, and Adagrad.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported IWSLT14 BLEU performance varies with learning-rate scaling; AdaHessian remains effective at larger scales where AdamW diverges. Block size changes produce small BLEU variations. Cifar10 accuracy varies modestly with Hessian computation frequency.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaHessian matches or improves benchmark generalization relative to the default optimizers and achieves lower transformer training losses or perplexities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects training objectives and generalization across vision, language, and recommendation tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 6 reports 32.48 ± 0.83 BLEU for AdaHessian at 10× its base learning rate, while AdamW diverges at 10× its own base rate. Neither initial stability thresholds nor loss-curvature recovery trajectories are measured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdaHessian tolerates larger multiples of its tuned base learning rate than AdamW on IWSLT14.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 reports convergence within seven iterations with Hessian momentum, versus failure to converge after 1,000 iterations without it, on a constructed scalar objective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian momentum can improve convergence on an objective with oscillatory local curvature.

record.problems: No training classification-error results are reported. The image-classification tables report final dataset accuracy, and the loss curves do not provide numerical training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows meet the required criterion: optimizer comparisons report other outcomes and do not measure the claim's training-error behavior or version-specific conditions.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error with SGD or Adam, including label corruption and effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Spurious-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and its dependence on extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth in plain networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified alternative training recipes.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
Learning rates relative to initial stability limits, transient loss growth with curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below the initial threshold.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate for these claim versions. References to residual networks and batch-normalization research do not supply controlled tests of V3 or V6. The record's relation='tests' conflicts with its otherwise correct exclusion rationale.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size effects, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher.
Plain versus residual depth comparisons, training classification error by depth, and the specified special initialization or normalization-free residual recipes.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, depth effects, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, and 10,000-layer plain CNN training.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss-curvature dynamics, and long-run sharpness behavior.
Batch-normalization comparisons for speed or learning-rate tolerance and Fixup residual training without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
